newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission says Boeing failing to meet EU fears.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission says Boeing failing to meet EU fears.

text.p: The European Commission on Tuesday said that Boeing had so far failed to address its competition concerns regarding the merger with McDonnell Douglas and that it fully backed the tough stance being taken by its antitrust chief.
"Boeing has so far not agreed to measures which would meet these concerns and achieve that objective," the Commission said in a statement.
The statement was the strongest indication to date from the Commission that it may block the $14 billion merger at its next weekly meeting on July 23.

"Unless the legitimate competition concerns of the Commission can be met and genuine choice maintained for purchasers of aircraft worldwide, the Commission could not approve the merger," the written statement by the Commission's spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said.

Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has expressed fears that the deal would strengthen Boeing's dominant position in the civil aviation market, although McDonnell Douglas has become a minor player.
Antitrust experts from the 15 EU states agreed unanimously on July 4 that the deal could not be allowed if the Commission's competition concerns were not addressed.
